title: The Classified Files
desc: Espionage, forgotten empires & the stories they left out of textbooks

questions.q: Operation Mincemeat was a WWII deception plan involving a dead body carrying fake documents. What was the corpse's fake identity?
questions.a: Major William Martin of the Royal Marines — the body was actually a Welsh tramp named Glyndwr Michael

questions.q: The Library of Alexandria's destruction is often blamed on a single fire. Why is that misleading?
questions.a: It declined gradually over centuries through multiple events — funding cuts, civil wars, and several fires, not one catastrophic moment

questions.q: Which empire at its peak controlled the largest contiguous land area in human history?
questions.a: The Mongol Empire under Genghis Khan and his successors — roughly 24 million km²

questions.q: The Voynich Manuscript, written in an unknown script, has never been deciphered. What century does it date from?
During the Cold War, the CIA spent millions on a programme to use cats as listening devices. What was it called?
questions.a: Acoustic Kitty — it was abandoned after the first cat was reportedly hit by a taxi

questions.q: The Rosetta Stone was key to decoding Egyptian hieroglyphics. But what three scripts does it actually contain?
Which 14th-century African emperor is considered the wealthiest person in history, adjusted for inflation?
questions.a: Mansa Musa of the Mali Empire — his hajj to Mecca in 1324 crashed gold prices across North Africa and the Middle East

questions.q: The 'Defenestration of Prague' triggered the Thirty Years' War. What does 'defenestration' literally mean?
questions.a: Throwing someone out of a window — Catholic officials were thrown from a Prague Castle window in 1618

questions.q: Project MKUltra was a real CIA programme. What was its purpose?
questions.a: Mind control experimentation — including dosing unwitting subjects with LSD (ran from the 1950s to 1973)

questions.q: The Doomsday Book, commissioned by William the Conqueror in 1086, was essentially what?
questions.a: A comprehensive survey and census of England's land, resources, and livestock — the first national audit
